papers.title: On Demand, Not Uniformity: Adaptive Expert Orchestration for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) enables Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to adapt to sequential instruction data while retaining previously acquired knowledge. While recent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based methods mitigate forgetting by freezing historical experts and introducing new ones, they largely overlook the varying adaptation demands across tasks. Probing incoming tasks reveals pronounced heterogeneity in layer-wise gradient pressure and token-wise prediction difficulty. This observation highlights two unresolved decisions: where additional capacity is needed and how strongly new experts should contribute to individual tokens. To address both questions, we propose the Coverage-Calibrated Expert Injection and Residual Arbitration framework (CIRA-MoE), which derives expert acceptance margins via learnable threshold routing to serve as a unified coverage signal. Specifically, historical acceptance evidence guides the selective injection of new experts into insufficiently covered layers. Meanwhile, relative evidence between historical and current experts modulates token-wise residual contributions, coupled with arbitration-consistent regularization to promote expert specialization. Comprehensive experiments on UCIT and CoIN demonstrate that CIRA-MoE outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in MCIT.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态持续指令微调（MCIT）使多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）能够适应序列化的指令数据，同时保留先前获得的知识。尽管近期基于混合专家（MoE）的方法通过冻结历史专家并引入新专家来缓解遗忘，但它们在很大程度上忽略了不同任务之间变化的适应需求。对传入任务的探测揭示了逐层梯度压力和逐token预测难度上的显著异质性。这一观察凸显了两个尚未解决的决策：何处需要额外容量，以及新专家应对单个token产生多强的贡献。为解决这两个问题，我们提出了覆盖校准专家注入与残差仲裁框架（CIRA-MoE），该框架通过可学习阈值路由推导专家接受边际，作为统一的覆盖信号。具体而言，历史接受证据指导将新专家选择性注入覆盖不足的层。同时，历史专家与当前专家之间的相对证据调节逐token的残差贡献，并结合仲裁一致性正则化以促进专家专业化。在UCIT和CoIN上的综合实验表明，CIRA-MoE在MCIT中优于现有最先进方法。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出CIRA-MoE框架，利用可学习阈值路由的覆盖信号指导新专家选择性注入覆盖不足的层，并按历史与当前专家的相对证据调节逐token残差贡献，在UCIT和CoIN上优于现有方法。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: The rise of the agentic web has been accompanied by growing demand for on-device Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that perform diverse cross-modal web tasks with enhanced privacy and reduced latency. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are widely adopted in modern VLMs for compute-efficient scalability, yet their multi-expert architecture poses deployment challenges due to substantial memory demands. Mixed-precision quantization is an effective compression technique that reduces bit-widths while adapting to the heterogeneous hardware budgets of edge devices, particularly well-suited for MoE due to its inherent structural sparsity, which causes imbalanced importance among experts. While prior work has applied quantization for efficient MoE inference at the edge, we point out that in MoE-based VLMs, the modality-specific characteristics of visual and text tokens further impact expert quantization. To address this issue, we present MoMoVL, a modality-aware adaptive compression framework for MoE-based VLMs that brings vision-language inference within reach of on-device resource budgets. Motivated by our empirical findings on modality-induced disparities across experts, MoMoVL jointly exploits the per-expert activation profile and per-modality quantization sensitivity to guide bit-width assignment. Experimental results show that MoMoVL improves the accuracy-compression trade-off relative to state-of-the-art mixed-precision baselines and reduces memory footprint by up to 15.44% with a modest drop in accuracy over its uniform-precision baseline. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/sco-edge/MoMoVL.
papers.abstract_zh: 智能体网络的兴起伴随着对设备端视觉语言模型（VLMs）日益增长的需求，这些模型以更强的隐私性和更低的延迟执行多样化的跨模态网络任务。混合专家（MoE）模型因其计算高效的扩展性而被现代VLMs广泛采用，但其多专家架构因巨大的内存需求而带来部署挑战。混合精度量化是一种有效的压缩技术，可在降低位宽的同时适应边缘设备的异构硬件预算，尤其适合MoE，因为其固有的结构稀疏性导致专家间重要性不均衡。尽管先前工作已将量化用于边缘高效MoE推理，但我们指出，在基于MoE的VLMs中，视觉token和文本token的模态特定特性会进一步影响专家量化。为解决这一问题，我们提出MoMoVL，一种面向基于MoE的VLMs的模态感知自适应压缩框架，使视觉语言推理进入设备端资源预算范围。受我们对专家间模态引发差异的实证发现启发，MoMoVL联合利用逐专家激活画像和逐模态量化敏感度来指导位宽分配。实验结果表明，相对于最先进的混合精度基线，MoMoVL改善了精度-压缩权衡，并相较其均匀精度基线将内存占用最多降低15.44%，精度仅有适度下降。我们的代码和数据公开于https://github.com/sco-edge/MoMoVL。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出MoMoVL模态感知自适应压缩框架，联合利用逐专家激活画像与逐模态量化敏感度分配位宽，在精度适度下降下将内存占用最多降低15.44%。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
papers.abstract_en: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. However, evaluating one quantized reasoning model takes tens of GPU-hours, and combining methods from different codebases means porting each to the new architecture by hand. We present QDA, a system in which an agent designs the recipe for each model and precision. To make evaluation fast, QDA scores each candidate in minutes by its output KL divergence from the original model on reasoning traces that the agent never sees, and checks promising ones with long generations to catch failures such as repetition loops. To make building fast, QDA provides a library of public PTQ methods that are compatible with one another and with new model architectures. Across four reasoning models, QDA improves accuracy over the strongest public recipe by 0.9, 1.4 and 2.2 percentage points on average at W4A16, W4A8 and W3A16, using 64 GPU-hours per search. On the 320B-parameter MoE model GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4 W4A4, it recovers 98.3% of the FP8 model's accuracy, against 96.9% for the best vendor checkpoint. Every QDA checkpoint also runs on existing serving kernels with no inference overhead. We will release the library, the evaluator and the harness.
papers.abstract_zh: 训练后量化是低成本服务大语言模型的标准方式。然而，最佳量化配方因模型和精度而异。因此，专家必须为每个新模型重新设计，这耗时且往往次优。幸运的是，LLM智能体可以通过多轮构建和评估候选来接管这一设计，使更多轮次带来更好的配方。然而，评估一个量化推理模型需要数十个GPU小时，而组合来自不同代码库的方法意味着需手工将每种方法移植到新架构。我们提出QDA，一个由智能体为每个模型和精度设计配方的系统。为加快评估，QDA通过在智能体从未见过的推理轨迹上计算候选相对原始模型的输出KL散度，在数分钟内为其打分，并用长生成检查有前景的候选以捕捉重复循环等失败。为加快构建，QDA提供相互兼容且兼容新模型架构的公开PTQ方法库。在四个推理模型上，QDA在W4A16、W4A8和W3A16下相较最强公开配方平均提升准确率0.9、1.4和2.2个百分点，每次搜索使用64 GPU小时。在320B参数的MoE模型GLM-5.3-Flash的NVFP4 W4A4下，它恢复了FP8模型准确率的98.3%，而最佳厂商检查点为96.9%。每个QDA检查点还可在现有服务内核上运行，无推理开销。我们将发布该库、评估器与测试框架。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出QDA系统，由LLM智能体通过KL散度快速评估与兼容PTQ方法库迭代设计量化配方，在四个推理模型上平均提升准确率最高2.2个百分点，并在GLM-5.3-Flash上恢复FP8准确率的98.3%。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
匹配 模型架构：model architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: SpatialMem: Building Quantitative Spatial Reasoning Agents with Hierarchical Memory
papers.abstract_en: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities in qualitative spatial reasoning, but remain limited in quantitative spatial reasoning. Current work leverages the VLM agent to invoke external vision tools to perform computation. However, these methods usually bind each functional requirement to a single predefined vision specialist, implicitly resulting in fixed and rigid tool pipelines. In practice, addressing diverse spatial scenarios and tasks demands a broader diversity in pipeline orchestration and vision specialist selection to achieve robust spatial reasoning. However, such diversity leads to a combinatorial execution space, making it challenging for the agent to orchestrate the optimal pipelines and specialists for different scenarios. In this work, we propose SpatialMem, a memory framework that enables a VLM agent to accumulate tool-use experience and leverage that memory to orchestrate vision specialists to solve the spatial reasoning problem. SpatialMem builds a two-level memory structure, with task memory capturing tool orchestration and scene memory capturing tool selection. It further introduces a dual-state trajectory optimization process to preserve successful tool experiences and refine suboptimal ones. Moreover, existing spatial reasoning benchmarks suffer from quality issues and limited coverage of scene types and tasks. To address these gap, we propose MetricBench, a benchmark covering both indoor and outdoor scenes and three quantitative spatial reasoning tasks. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on MetricBench, Q-Spatial, and SpatilRGPT-Bench, outperforming best VLM baselines by 32% on MetricBench. Additionally, the memory design yields a 9.1% absolute gain over a memory-free agent on MetricBench.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）在定性空间推理方面已展现出显著能力，但在定量空间推理方面仍然有限。当前工作利用 VLM 智能体调用外部视觉工具来执行计算。然而，这些方法通常将每个功能需求绑定到单个预定义的视觉专家，隐式地导致固定且僵化的工具流水线。在实践中，应对多样的空间场景和任务需要更丰富的流水线编排与视觉专家选择多样性，以实现稳健的空间推理。然而，这种多样性导致组合式的执行空间，使智能体难以为不同场景编排最优的流水线与专家。在本工作中，我们提出 SpatialMem，一种记忆框架，使 VLM 智能体能够积累工具使用经验，并利用该记忆编排视觉专家以解决空间推理问题。SpatialMem 构建两级记忆结构，任务记忆捕获工具编排，场景记忆捕获工具选择。它进一步引入双状态轨迹优化过程，以保留成功的工具经验并改进次优经验。此外，现有空间推理基准存在质量问题，且对场景类型和任务的覆盖有限。为弥补这一空白，我们提出 MetricBench，一个覆盖室内和室外场景以及三项定量空间推理任务的基准。我们的方法在 MetricBench、Q-Spatial 和 SpatilRGPT-Bench 上取得最先进结果，在 MetricBench 上比最佳 VLM 基线高出 32%。此外，该记忆设计在 MetricBench 上比无记忆智能体取得 9.1% 的绝对增益。
papers.tldr_zh: SpatialMem 通过任务记忆与场景记忆两级结构及双状态轨迹优化，让 VLM 智能体积累工具使用经验以编排视觉专家，并在新基准 MetricBench 上比最佳基线高 32%。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Beam Model Technical Report
papers.abstract_en: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters, specifically built and optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam delivers frontier level reasoning, while requiring 3-4x less inference compute than many models of its class. Pretrained on 23.8T diverse, curated, high-quality tokens, Beam features a 1M-token context window achieved through a novel two-stage midtraining phase, built on verifiable, correctness-anchored data. Post-training leveraged a large-scale, fully asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) campaign across 10.5K GB300 GPUs, generating over 100M rollouts over 4 weeks of training. We believe this is one of the largest scale RL runs conducted by any open lab to date. Across our evaluation suite, capabilities continued to improve as we increased RL compute, with no sign of a plateau. Supported by deep hardware-model co-design, FP8/NVFP4 quantization, and a 1.93B-parameter speculative decoding drafter (DFlash 2), Beam maximizes serving throughput with efficient, flexible deployment. Averaged across conversation turns and harm categories, Beam refuses or pivots on 88.9% of harmful requests while complying with 81.5% of harmless requests, achieving the highest refusal/pivot rate on harmful requests among open-weight models on the Pareto frontier.
papers.abstract_zh: Beam 是一个稀疏混合专家（MoE）模型，总参数 501.3B、激活参数 23.4B，专门针对编码、推理和智能体工作负载构建并优化。Beam 提供前沿水平的推理能力，同时所需推理计算量比同类许多模型少 3-4 倍。Beam 在 23.8T 多样、精选的高质量 token 上预训练，通过新颖的两阶段中期训练阶段实现 1M token 上下文窗口，该阶段建立在可验证、以正确性为锚的数据之上。后训练利用跨 10.5K 块 GB300 GPU 的大规模全异步强化学习（RL）训练，在 4 周训练中生成超过 1 亿次 rollout。我们相信这是迄今任何开放实验室开展的最大规模 RL 运行之一。在我们的评估套件中，随着 RL 计算量增加，能力持续提升，没有出现平台期迹象。在深度软硬件协同设计、FP8/NVFP4 量化以及 1.93B 参数投机解码草稿模型（DFlash 2）的支持下，Beam 以高效、灵活的部署最大化服务吞吐量。在对话轮次和危害类别上平均而言，Beam 对 88.9% 的有害请求予以拒绝或转移，同时对 81.5% 的无害请求予以遵从，在帕累托前沿的开放权重模型中实现了对有害请求最高的拒绝/转移率。
papers.tldr_zh: Beam 是总参数 501.3B、激活 23.4B 的稀疏 MoE 模型，经 23.8T token 预训练、两阶段中期训练获得 1M 上下文，并在 10.5K 块 GB300 GPU 上完成大规模异步 RL 后训练。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
匹配 效率：quantization, speculative decoding
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
papers.abstract_en: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question ends if the answer is unchanged and confident. Otherwise, the agent's large model verifies and corrects the glimpse without tools, and their answers are fused. Only questions that still lack evidence reach the agent, in one forward pass that SpecLook-Fast skips, so no question runs the loop. The trace scores every answer's reliability without labels. Extensive experiments on V*, HR-Bench, and POPE show that both are more accurate than every baseline on every split. SpecLook reaches 87.2% and 86.2% mean accuracy with 7.7x and 4.7x speedups over the DeepEyes-7B and Thyme-RL agents, and SpecLook-Fast reaches 9.9x and 6.3x.
papers.abstract_zh: 以图像思考的智能体多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）将推理与放大工具调用交错进行。然而，这一顺序循环速度慢，且其答案不携带可靠性分数。先前对token、推理步骤或答案的推测仍保留该循环，且答案推测还会接受自信的错误。我们发现该循环大多只增加一个放大步骤，而小模型在大多数划分上领先于智能体。我们的关键洞见是推测智能体的下一个观察，与草拟答案不同，该观察可被验证、纠正并用于检验答案。我们提出SpecLook，一个免训练的三级推测-验证框架。小模型草拟一个瞥见并据此重新作答，若答案不变且置信则问题结束。否则，智能体的大模型在无工具条件下验证并纠正该瞥见，并融合二者的答案。只有仍缺乏证据的问题才到达智能体，且仅需一次前向传播，SpecLook-Fast会跳过该传播，因此没有问题是运行循环的。该轨迹无需标签即可为每个答案的可靠性打分。在V*、HR-Bench和POPE上的大量实验表明，二者在每个划分上均比所有基线更准确。SpecLook在DeepEyes-7B和Thyme-RL智能体上分别以7.7倍和4.7倍加速达到87.2%和86.2%的平均准确率，SpecLook-Fast则达到9.9倍和6.3倍。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出免训练的SpecLook推测-验证框架，通过小模型草拟并验证智能体的下一个观察而非答案，在V*、HR-Bench和POPE上以最高9.9倍加速取得更高准确率。

papers.title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract_en: We propose VC-VQA, a large-scale benchmark for vision-centric knowledge reasoning, aiming to systematically evaluate the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition and complex multi-stage reasoning. Unlike existing benchmarks that primarily treat visual information as entity recognition and rely on text-based external knowledge, VC-VQA explicitly models the role of visual information by considering both its source (internal vs. external images) and stage of involvement (pre-retrieval vs. post-retrieval). Specifically, VC-VQA requires models to retrieve external visual evidence, identify visual clues before retrieval, and localize, verify, or match retrieved knowledge against the internal image. We further construct a controlled multimodal knowledge base with traceable textual and visual evidence for each sample. We evaluate 21 representative MLLMs under four settings: no external knowledge, with provided evidence, knowledge base retrieval, and open-web search. Experimental results lead to three key findings: current models still struggle with vision-centric knowledge reasoning; fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition remains the primary bottleneck; and agentic retrieval highlights the value of multi-step planning and cross-modal knowledge integration. Overall, VC-VQA provides a more challenging benchmark for evaluating vision-centric knowledge reasoning in MLLMs. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/CASIA-IVA-Lab/VC-VQA.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出 VC-VQA，一个面向视觉中心知识推理的大规模基准，旨在系统评估多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在细粒度视觉知识获取和复杂多阶段推理方面的能力。与主要将视觉信息视为实体识别并依赖文本外部知识的现有基准不同，VC-VQA 通过同时考虑视觉信息的来源（内部图像与外部图像）和参与阶段（检索前与检索后）来显式建模视觉信息的作用。具体而言，VC-VQA 要求模型检索外部视觉证据、在检索前识别视觉线索，并将检索到的知识与内部图像进行定位、验证或匹配。我们进一步为每个样本构建了带有可追溯文本和视觉证据的受控多模态知识库。我们在四种设置下评估了 21 个代表性 MLLM：无外部知识、提供证据、知识库检索和开放网络搜索。实验结果得出三个关键发现：当前模型在视觉中心知识推理方面仍存在困难；细粒度视觉知识获取仍是主要瓶颈；智能体式检索凸显了多步规划和跨模态知识整合的价值。总体而言，VC-VQA 为评估 MLLM 的视觉中心知识推理提供了一个更具挑战性的基准。我们的代码和数据集见 https://github.com/CASIA-IVA-Lab/VC-VQA。
papers.tldr_zh: VC-VQA 基准按视觉信息来源与参与阶段建模视觉中心知识推理，在四种设置下评估 21 个 MLLM，发现细粒度视觉知识获取是主要瓶颈。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration
papers.abstract_en: Images under non-uniform coupled degradations require diverse restoration capabilities for different degraded regions. Existing methods employ globally uniform operations, potentially overlooking regional differences and causing incomplete restoration or even damage to image content. Moreover, a degraded region may require successive restoration actions, and earlier actions may alter residual degradation characteristics or introduce artifacts, potentially hindering subsequent restoration. To address these challenges, we propose RegionAgent, an adaptive restoration framework that trains a Vision-Language Model (VLM) through two-stage preference learning to generate a region-specific restoration action at each iteration. Specifically, we first train the VLM to select an action suited to the current region through step-level Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), using preferences derived from immediate restoration feedback to supervise only the differing component in each action pair. To account for the effects of current actions on subsequent restoration, we then apply trajectory-level DPO, using preferences derived from complete trajectory scores to supervise the sole differing action in each trajectory pair. Furthermore, as conventional image-pair datasets do not directly provide preferences over regional restoration decisions, we construct a regional restoration preference dataset comprising 10K action pairs and 20K trajectory pairs for two-stage VLM training. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate strong restoration performance under both mixed and single degradations. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of two-stage preference learning in improving restoration quality.
papers.abstract_zh: 在非均匀耦合退化下的图像需要针对不同退化区域采用多样的复原能力。现有方法采用全局统一操作，可能忽略区域差异，导致复原不完整甚至损坏图像内容。此外，一个退化区域可能需要连续多个复原动作，而较早的动作可能改变残余退化特征或引入伪影，从而可能阻碍后续复原。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 RegionAgent，一种自适应复原框架，通过两阶段偏好学习训练视觉语言模型（VLM），在每次迭代中生成区域特定的复原动作。具体而言，我们首先通过步骤级直接偏好优化（DPO）训练 VLM 选择适合当前区域的动作，其偏好来自即时复原反馈，仅监督每个动作对中不同的组成部分。为考虑当前动作对后续复原的影响，我们随后应用轨迹级 DPO，其偏好来自完整轨迹得分，仅监督每个轨迹对中唯一不同的动作。此外，由于传统图像对数据集不直接提供区域复原决策的偏好，我们构建了一个区域复原偏好数据集，包含 10K 动作对和 20K 轨迹对，用于两阶段 VLM 训练。在多个数据集上的实验表明，在混合和单一退化下均具有强复原性能。消融研究进一步验证了两阶段偏好学习在提升复原质量方面的有效性。
papers.tldr_zh: RegionAgent 用步骤级与轨迹级两阶段 DPO 训练 VLM 逐次生成区域特定复原动作，并构建 10K 动作对与 20K 轨迹对偏好数据集。

papers.title: Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract_en: GPUs are expensive, yet latency-critical large language model (LLM) inference leaves part of them idle. Colocation reclaims this capacity by running best-effort work, such as fine-tuning, alongside serving. Many leading LLMs now use a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which adds a new source of idle time. Under expert parallelism, MoE experts are spread across GPUs, and because the router sends uneven numbers of tokens to each GPU, lightly loaded GPUs wait for the most loaded one. Even after applying load balancing solutions, such bubbles still take 8--13% of prefill time. We present BubbleTea, the first colocation system that leverages expert-parallel bubbles for fine-tuning. Unlike existing colocation systems, which make one scheduling decision for all GPUs per forward pass, BubbleTea predicts each GPU's bubble at every layer from the router's token assignment, and fills it with short chunks of fine-tuning work that reuse the weights already loaded for serving. We also introduce compiler passes that automatically derive these chunks from the served LLM as-is, without porting each model architecture to a separate training engine. Our evaluation on three MoE models, served on four A100 GPUs, shows that fine-tuning throughput with BubbleTea is 1.9--6.2$\times$ faster than with LLMStation, a state-of-the-art colocation system. BubbleTea keeps p90 inference latency within 10% of serving alone in 50 of 63 workloads, compared to 44 for LLMStation. On bursty production traces, BubbleTea trains 3.3$\times$ faster than LLMStation and 14$\times$ faster than a stock trainer colocated under CUDA MPS, with p90 inference latency staying within 7% of serving alone.
papers.abstract_zh: GPU昂贵，然而延迟关键的大语言模型（LLM）推理使部分GPU处于空闲。共置通过运行尽力而为的工作（如微调）与服务工作负载并行来回收这一容量。许多领先LLM现采用混合专家（MoE）架构，这增加了新的空闲时间来源。在专家并行下，MoE专家分布在各GPU上，且由于路由器向每个GPU发送的token数不均，轻负载GPU需等待负载最重的GPU。即使应用负载均衡方案，此类气泡仍占预填充时间的8--13%。我们提出BubbleTea，首个利用专家并行气泡进行微调的共置系统。与现有共置系统每次前向传播对所有GPU做一次调度决策不同，BubbleTea根据路由器的token分配预测每个GPU在每一层的气泡，并用复用已为服务加载权重的短微调工作块填充它。我们还引入编译器遍，可自动从原样服务的LLM推导这些工作块，而无需将每个模型架构移植到单独的训练引擎。我们在四块A100 GPU上服务三个MoE模型的评估表明，BubbleTea的微调吞吐量比最先进共置系统LLMStation快1.9--6.2倍。BubbleTea在63个工作负载中的50个上将p90推理延迟保持在单独服务的10%以内，而LLMStation为44个。在突发生产轨迹上，BubbleTea训练速度比LLMStation快3.3倍，比在CUDA MPS下共置的现成训练器快14倍，且p90推理延迟保持在单独服务的7%以内。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出BubbleTea共置系统，按路由器token分配逐层预测各GPU的专家并行气泡并填充复用服务权重的微调工作块，微调吞吐量比LLMStation快1.9--6.2倍。

匹配 模型架构：model architecture

papers.title: Reference-Guided Data Curation for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pretraining
papers.abstract_en: Training 3D vision-language models (VLMs) on large medical imaging datasets collected across institutions is constrained by data quality. Vast, uncurated pools of image-report pairs are characterized by redundancy, class imbalance, and cross-institutional heterogeneity. We address this challenge of data curation for improving 3D VLM pretraining by proposing an offline, training-free, reference-guided data curation recipe. Our approach leverages a small, high-quality reference set to independently extract quality signals for each modality of a large, uncurated pool and merges them through a rank-aggregation step into a single ranking that guides sample selection. We validate this method on datasets comprising 35k 3D abdominal CT volume-report pairs from two institutions and 58k 2D chest X-ray image-report pairs. On 3D CT, using our reference-guided data curation strategy, our curated model matches the zero-shot disease classification performance of a state-of-the-art baseline (Merlin) while using $3.3\times$ less training data and a reference set of 5k samples. On 2D chest X-rays, our method yields a curated model that matches or exceeds the zero-shot disease classification performance of a model trained on the full pool while using up to $10\times$ less training data and a reference set of only 74 samples. Ablations show that the selection is stable under resampling of the reference, that smaller reference sets still outperform random sampling, and that label rebalancing does not improve performance. To support reproducibility, we release our code.
papers.abstract_zh: 在跨机构收集的大规模医学影像数据集上训练3D视觉-语言模型（VLM）受限于数据质量。大量未经整理的图像-报告对具有冗余、类别不平衡和跨机构异质性等特点。我们针对改进3D VLM预训练的数据整理难题，提出一种离线、免训练、参考引导的数据整理方案。该方法利用一个小规模高质量参考集，为大规模未整理池中每个模态独立提取质量信号，并通过秩聚合步骤将其合并为单一排序以指导样本选择。我们在包含来自两个机构的35k个3D腹部CT体数据-报告对以及58k个2D胸部X射线图像-报告对的数据集上验证了该方法。在3D CT上，采用我们的参考引导数据整理策略，整理后的模型在使用3.3倍更少训练数据和5k样本参考集的情况下，达到了最先进基线（Merlin）的零样本疾病分类性能。在2D胸部X射线上，我们的方法得到的整理模型在使用最多10倍更少训练数据和仅74个样本的参考集的情况下，达到或超过在全量池上训练模型的零样本疾病分类性能。消融实验表明，选择在参考集重采样下是稳定的，更小的参考集仍优于随机采样，且标签重平衡并未提升性能。为支持可复现性，我们发布了代码。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出一种离线免训练的参考引导数据整理方法，利用小规模高质量参考集为大规模未整理医学图像-报告对生成质量排序以筛选样本，在3D腹部CT和2D胸部X射线数据上以显著更少的训练数据达到或超过基线零样本疾病分类性能。

papers.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) can correctly interpret physics diagrams yet apply constraints outside the states or conditions in which they hold, causing premise errors to propagate through subsequent calculations. We introduce PhysScope, an inference-time visual harness that supports self-correction of these scope mismatches without updating model weights. PhysScope enables the model to link physical scopes directly to its visual observations and explicitly constructs derived views to support reasoning. The harness imposes explicit constraints on state distinctions, conditions, and physical scopes during model reasoning, and checks agent-proposed revisions against sources and scopes. Accepted revisions invalidate registered dependents, thereby maintaining scope-aware working memory. On PhysAlign, PhysScope achieves higher solving scores than direct solving across all six evaluated VLMs. With Gemini-3.8-flash, it outperforms Canvas-CoT by 9.34 percentage points and substantially improves solving accuracy on the out-of-distribution (OOD) PhysUniBench benchmark. Ablation studies support explicit scope management and dependency maintenance as design principles for multimodal physics reasoning agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）能够正确解读物理示意图，却会在其约束不成立的状态或条件之外应用这些约束，导致前提错误传播到后续计算中。我们提出 PhysScope，一种推理时视觉支架，支持在不更新模型权重的情况下对这些范围不匹配进行自我纠正。PhysScope 使模型能够将物理范围直接关联到其视觉观察，并显式构建派生视图以支持推理。该支架在模型推理过程中对状态区分、条件和物理范围施加显式约束，并对照来源和范围检查智能体提出的修订。被接受的修订会使已注册的依赖项失效，从而维持范围感知的工作记忆。在 PhysAlign 上，PhysScope 在全部六个被评估的 VLM 上取得比直接求解更高的求解得分。使用 Gemini-3.8-flash 时，它比 Canvas-CoT 高出 9.34 个百分点，并在分布外（OOD）的 PhysUniBench 基准上大幅提升求解准确率。消融研究支持显式范围管理和依赖维护作为多模态物理推理智能体的设计原则。
papers.tldr_zh: PhysScope 作为推理时视觉支架，显式约束物理范围并维护依赖关系以自我纠正前提错误，在 PhysAlign 上六个 VLM 均优于直接求解，Gemini-3.8-flash 下比 Canvas-CoT 高 9.34 个百分点。

papers.title: Ultimate3D: Teaching Multimodal LLMs 3D Camera-Object Relations by Large-Scale Visual Instruction Data
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) struggle with accurately capturing camera-object relations, especially for object orientation, camera viewpoint, and camera shots. This stems from the fact that existing MLLMs are trained on images with limited diverse camera-object relations and corresponding textual descriptions. To address this, we propose a synthetic generation pipeline to create large-scale 3D visual instruction datasets. Our framework takes 3D assets as input and uses rendering and diffusion-based image generation models to create photorealistic images preserving precise camera-object relations. Additionally, large language models (LLMs) are used to generate text prompts for guiding visual instruction tuning and controlling image generation. We create Ultimate3D, a large-scale 3D-grounded 2D visual instruction dataset. Ultimate3D consists of 240K VQAs with precise camera-object annotations, and corresponding benchmark. MLLMs fine-tuned on our proposed dataset outperform commercial models by a large margin, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 29.7% on camera-object relation recognition tasks. Our code, dataset, and benchmark will contribute to broad MLLM applications.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在准确捕捉相机-物体关系方面存在困难，尤其是物体朝向、相机视角和相机镜头类型。这源于现有MLLM训练所用图像中相机-物体关系多样性有限且缺乏相应文本描述。为解决这一问题，我们提出一种合成生成流水线，用于创建大规模3D视觉指令数据集。我们的框架以3D资产为输入，使用渲染和基于扩散的图像生成模型来创建保持精确相机-物体关系的照片级真实图像。此外，使用大语言模型（LLM）生成文本提示，以指导视觉指令微调并控制图像生成。我们构建了Ultimate3D，一个大规模基于3D的2D视觉指令数据集。Ultimate3D包含240K个具有精确相机-物体标注的VQA，以及相应的基准。在我们提出的数据集上微调的MLLM大幅优于商业模型，在相机-物体关系识别任务上平均准确率提升29.7%。我们的代码、数据集和基准将有助于广泛的MLLM应用。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出以3D资产为输入的合成生成流水线，结合渲染、扩散模型和LLM生成保持精确相机-物体关系的图像与文本指令，构建含240K VQA的Ultimate3D数据集及基准，微调后的MLLM在相机-物体关系识别任务上平均准确率提升29.7%。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: DAQ: Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Spiking transformers combine attention-based representation learning with sparse spike communication, yet their weights and membrane variables still incur substantial storage and computation overhead. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical way to reduce these overheads, but preserving neuronal firing under weight and membrane quantization remains challenging. In this paper, we propose Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization (DAQ), a method that calibrates the quantizers to align neuronal firing decisions with those of a floating-point reference. We analyze how errors from these quantizers affect firing at decision boundaries and how they propagate over time steps in recurrent neurons. Based on this analysis, we formulate an objective that encourages quantized membrane variables to remain within the reference firing regions along the quantized model's own state trajectory. Experiments across multiple spiking transformer architectures on image classification, semantic segmentation, and event-based tracking demonstrate the effectiveness of DAQ with 4-bit weights and membrane variables. On FE108, DAQ achieves 58.8\% AUC and 90.9\% PR with SDTrack, while reducing energy by 66.2\%.
papers.abstract_zh: 脉冲Transformer将基于注意力的表示学习与稀疏脉冲通信相结合，但其权重和膜变量仍带来大量存储与计算开销。训练后量化（PTQ）为降低这些开销提供了实用途径，但在权重和膜量化下保持神经元发放仍具挑战。本文提出决策对齐训练后量化（Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization, DAQ），一种通过校准量化器使神经元发放决策与浮点参考对齐的方法。我们分析了这些量化器的误差如何影响决策边界处的发放，以及误差如何在循环神经元中随时间步传播。基于该分析，我们构建了一个目标，促使量化后的膜变量沿量化模型自身的状态轨迹保持在参考发放区域内。在图像分类、语义分割和基于事件的跟踪任务上跨多种脉冲Transformer架构的实验表明，DAQ 在 4 位权重和膜变量下有效。在 FE108 上，DAQ 配合 SDTrack 取得 58.8% AUC 和 90.9% PR，同时降低 66.2% 能耗。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出决策对齐训练后量化DAQ，通过校准量化器使脉冲发放决策对齐浮点参考并约束膜变量沿自身状态轨迹处于参考发放区域，在4位权重与膜变量下于分类、分割和事件跟踪任务上有效，FE108上降低66.2%能耗。

papers.title: Life-IQA+: Boosting Blind Image Quality Assessment via GCN-enhanced Layer Interaction and Flexible Hierarchical Expert Specialization
papers.abstract_en: Blind image quality assessment (BIQA) is essential for evaluating and optimizing visual experience. Existing BIQA methods typically aggregate features from multiple backbone stages without accounting for their unequal contributions to quality prediction. Furthermore, uniformly supervising all experts may constrain their flexibility and limit the diversity of the learned quality representations. To address these issues, we present Life-IQA+, a quality representation decoding framework that combines graph convolutional network (GCN) enhanced layer interaction and flexible hierarchical expert specialization. Specifically, the layer interaction module constructs quality queries from GCN-refined deepest-stage features and uses penultimate-stage features as keys and values, thereby enabling cross-layer representation interaction via the cross-attention mechanism. Building on these representations, we further introduce a flexible hierarchical mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture comprising a densely activated shared expert layer and a sparsely activated routed expert layer. To enhance the representation diversity and ability of experts, we apply auxiliary classification supervision to a subset of shared experts using distortion-type labels for synthetic datasets and discretized quality-level labels for authentic datasets. Experiments on synthetic and authentic distortion benchmarks, together with controlled ablations of expert configurations and supervision strategies, show that Life-IQA+ achieves competitive prediction accuracy with a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost. The code is available at: https://github.com/TANGLONG2/Life-IQA-PlusPlus.
papers.abstract_zh: 盲图像质量评估（BIQA）对于评估和优化视觉体验至关重要。现有 BIQA 方法通常聚合来自多个骨干阶段的特征，却未考虑它们对质量预测的不等贡献。此外，对所有专家进行统一监督可能限制其灵活性，并限制所学质量表示的多样性。为解决这些问题，我们提出 Life-IQA+，一个质量表示解码框架，结合了图卷积网络（GCN）增强的层交互与灵活的分层专家专业化。具体而言，层交互模块从 GCN 精炼的最深阶段特征构建质量查询，并将倒数第二阶段的特征作为键和值，从而通过交叉注意力机制实现跨层表示交互。在这些表示的基础上，我们进一步引入灵活的分层混合专家（MoE）架构，包含密集激活的共享专家层和稀疏激活的路由专家层。为增强专家的表示多样性和能力，我们对一部分共享专家施加辅助分类监督，对合成数据集使用失真类型标签，对真实数据集使用离散化质量等级标签。在合成与真实失真基准上的实验，以及对专家配置和监督策略的受控消融，表明 Life-IQA+ 在预测准确率上具有竞争力，并在准确率与计算成本之间取得良好平衡。代码见：https://github.com/TANGLONG2/Life-IQA-PlusPlus。
papers.tldr_zh: Life-IQA+ 通过 GCN 增强的跨层交互与分层混合专家架构解码质量表示，并对部分共享专家施加辅助分类监督，在合成与真实失真基准上取得有竞争力的准确率与计算成本平衡。

papers.title: Learning to Think with Images Faithfully via Adaptive Data Selection
papers.abstract_en: Thinking with images (TwI) empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to overcome perceptual bottlenecks by actively cropping and zooming into fine-grained visual details, promising both higher accuracy and interpretable, region-grounded reasoning. However, our analysis shows that the improved accuracy of TwI models does not guarantee faithful tool use; they frequently invoke tools without actually relying on the zoomed region, undermining the reliability of tool-assisted reasoning. We trace this unfaithful behaviour to the training data: when questions are answerable without zooming, the model can answer correctly while ignoring the returned evidence, and this problem is exacerbated during training as the model becomes better at answering without tools. To keep zooming useful throughout training, we adapt the training data to the model's evolving capability and train on questions where correct zoomed evidence can still help the model answer correctly. This selection is supported by a data synthesis pipeline that localises small objects and constructs verifiable questions about their fine details, and complemented by an adaptiveness reward that favours tool-free answers when zooming is unnecessary. The experimental results show that our method substantially improves reasoning faithfulness and achieves state-of-the-art performance on visual search benchmarks (+11.6% on V*, +7.9% on HR-Bench 4K, and +9.4% on HR-Bench 8K). On multimodal hallucination benchmarks, our model also outperforms the compared TwI baselines. These results suggest that improving TwI faithfulness does not sacrifice accuracy and that both can be learnt from the right training data without directly supervising the reasoning process.
papers.abstract_zh: 用图像思考（TwI）使视觉语言模型（VLM）能够通过主动裁剪和放大细粒度视觉细节来克服感知瓶颈，有望同时带来更高准确率和可解释的、基于区域的推理。然而，我们的分析表明，TwI 模型准确率的提升并不保证忠实的工具使用；它们经常调用工具却并未真正依赖放大区域，从而削弱了工具辅助推理的可靠性。我们将这种不忠实行为追溯到训练数据：当问题无需放大即可回答时，模型可以忽略返回的证据而正确作答，并且随着模型越来越擅长无工具作答，这一问题在训练中会加剧。为使放大在整个训练过程中保持有用，我们根据模型不断演进的能力调整训练数据，并在正确放大证据仍能帮助模型正确作答的问题上进行训练。这一选择由一个数据合成流程支持，该流程定位小物体并围绕其细粒度细节构建可验证问题，并辅以自适应性奖励，在放大不必要时偏好无工具作答。实验结果表明，我们的方法显著提升了推理忠实性，并在视觉搜索基准上达到最先进性能（V* 上 +11.6%，HR-Bench 4K 上 +7.9%，HR-Bench 8K 上 +9.4%）。在多模态幻觉基准上，我们的模型也优于所比较的 TwI 基线。这些结果表明，提升 TwI 忠实性不会牺牲准确率，且二者均可从正确的训练数据中习得，而无需直接监督推理过程。
papers.tldr_zh: 该方法根据模型能力自适应选择训练数据并加入自适应性奖励，使 TwI 模型在需要时真正依赖放大区域，在提升推理忠实性的同时于视觉搜索基准上取得最先进准确率。

papers.title: NaviGATE: Noise-Aware Dual-View Generation for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal knowledge graph reasoning (MKGR) aims to infer missing facts by jointly exploiting relational structures, textual descriptions, and visual evidence. Existing embedding-based methods effectively capture graph topology, but their fixed multimodal representations are less effective for query-specific fine-grained semantic reasoning, while generation-based methods are vulnerable to noisy retrieval and may produce invalid entities. To address these challenges, we propose NaviGATE, a noise-aware generative framework for MKGR. NaviGATE first aligns graph-derived structural representations with textual semantics, then performs structure-aware internal knowledge activation by fine-tuning the multimodal language model with multimodal entity summaries and injected structural tokens. In the noise-aware dual-view instruction tuning stage, NaviGATE jointly optimizes retrieval-free and retrieval-aware views: reliable retrieved candidates are reinforced through contrastive logit sharpening, while misleading candidates are suppressed through parametric consistency distillation. In inference, structure-constrained decoding restricts generation to valid entities in the target knowledge graph. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that NaviGATE consistently outperforms strong unimodal, multimodal, and generation-based baselines, and remains robust under noisy retrieval scenarios.

papers.title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Looped vision-language models (VLMs) deepen computation by reusing shared layers, approaching larger models' capabilities with fewer parameters and easing the storage and deployment burden of stacking independent layers. However, repeatedly processing long visual sequences still incurs substantial compute and GPU memory costs. Visual token compression reduces these costs by shortening sequences. Existing methods mainly select original tokens directly or combine selection with aggregation. In looped models, the former may overlook changing token importance across calls and discard information needed later; the latter lack joint consideration of output changes across calls, limiting information preservation. We propose LoopZip, a training-free visual token compression algorithm addressing both issues. Visual aggregation builds a compact candidate pool before the looped backbone, and cross-invocation selection averages instruction attention from the first two existing calls of the same shared attention layer to retain tokens needed by both states. Weight-tied value correction then jointly fits shared visual-value adjustments to both pre-selection layer outputs, reducing output deviations across states. To validate LoopZip's effectiveness, we conduct extensive experiments covering two open-source looped VLMs, eleven benchmarks, and three pruning ratios. On LoopVL-1B, LoopZip retains 97.16% of the original model's performance at 50% pruning ratio and exceeds the strongest baseline by 5.36% at 87.5% pruning ratio. Across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang, LoopVL-1B with LoopZip reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 58.36%-58.98% and achieves 2.01-2.47x end-to-end speedups over the original model.
papers.abstract_zh: 循环视觉语言模型（VLM）通过复用共享层来加深计算，以更少参数逼近更大模型的能力，并缓解堆叠独立层带来的存储与部署负担。然而，反复处理长视觉序列仍会带来大量计算和 GPU 内存开销。视觉 token 压缩通过缩短序列来降低这些开销。现有方法主要直接选择原始 token，或将选择与聚合相结合。在循环模型中，前者可能忽略不同调用间 token 重要性的变化，并丢弃后续所需的信息；后者缺乏对不同调用间输出变化的联合考虑，限制了信息保留。我们提出 LoopZip，一种无需训练的视觉 token 压缩算法，同时解决上述两个问题。视觉聚合在循环主干之前构建紧凑候选池，跨调用选择对同一共享注意力层前两次现有调用的指令注意力取平均，以保留两种状态都需要的 token。权重共享的值校正随后联合拟合共享视觉值调整，使其同时适配选择前层的两种输出，从而减小不同状态间的输出偏差。为验证 LoopZip 的有效性，我们开展了大量实验，覆盖两个开源循环 VLM、十一个基准和三种剪枝比例。在 LoopVL-1B 上，LoopZip 在 50% 剪枝比例下保留原模型 97.16% 的性能，在 87.5% 剪枝比例下超过最强基线 5.36%。在 Hugging Face Transformers、vLLM 和 SGLang 上，使用 LoopZip 的 LoopVL-1B 将峰值分配 GPU 内存降低 58.36%-58.98%，并相较原模型实现 2.01-2.47 倍端到端加速。
papers.tldr_zh: LoopZip 是一种无需训练的视觉 token 压缩方法，通过循环前视觉聚合、跨调用注意力平均选择和权重共享值校正，在循环 VLM 上以 50% 剪枝保留 97.16% 性能并显著降低显存与加速推理。

papers.title: RemoteVLPG: How to Obtain a Specific VLM for Language-Guided Path Generation on Remote Sensing Images?
papers.abstract_en: We study how to obtain a task-specific Vision-Language Model (VLM) for language-guided path generation between start and end points on remote sensing images. We explore this question from three aspects. First, we implement three widely used architectural approaches and compare their performance. Second, we design a scalable method for constructing pre-training data and build an effective pre-training dataset with a degree of diversity. Methods trained on this dataset achieve promising zero-shot performance. Third, we construct three benchmarks that support stratified evaluation and design three metrics for path generation. We investigate this problem through extensive experiments. The results show that the zero-shot performance of methods trained on the constructed pre-training dataset can exceed that of some advanced commercial VLMs. Code and Dataset can be available at https://github.com/jzdang/RemoteVLPG

papers.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract_en: Tree-structured speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models (VLMs) by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. However, long visual contexts increase the cost of speculative computation, making candidate coverage and redundant expansion important considerations beyond tree topology adaptation. We propose Raptor, a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort. Our key insight is that acceptance length alone cannot distinguish insufficient candidate coverage from excessive deep expansion, and these conditions require different allocation decisions. Raptor therefore extracts complementary rejection-aware signals to characterize speculative progress, frontier coverage, and redundant expansion. These signals jointly guide bounded, momentum-smoothed updates of tree depth, branching width, and drafting budget, together with execution control that limits unnecessary drafting and progressively restores expansion when appropriate. Extensive experiments with two VLMs across seven multimodal benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of Raptor, achieving up to 2.39x average speedup over autoregressive decoding.

papers.title: Goal-Guided Reinforcement Learning via Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Exploration remains a major challenge for reinforcement learning (RL) agents in Craftax-style environments due to sparse rewards and long horizons. Large language models (LLMs) can guide exploration by generating high-level goals, but methods using models without explicit task adaptation often rely on carefully designed prompts and may produce inconsistent or contextually inappropriate goals. We introduce CCGP-2M, a multimodal goal-preference dataset constructed from interaction trajectories in Craftax-Classic, and propose a vision-language model (VLM)-guided RL framework that learns environment-specific goal guidance from this dataset. The framework consists of two stages: offline VLM fine-tuning and online goal-guided RL. In the offline stage, we align the VLM with goal preferences using Kullback-Leibler Token-level Direct Preference Optimization (KLTDPO), which combines token-level KL regularization with distributionally robust reweighting. Experiments on Craftax-Classic show that our method collects diamonds earlier than state-of-the-art baselines, achieves the highest score and reward, and attains the highest success rates on most achievements.

papers.title: VidToC: Rethinking Video Token Compression for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Extending multimodal large language models (MLLMs) from images to videos faces substantial memory and latency challenges due to the massive number of visual tokens. These challenges have driven the development of numerous visual token compression methods and more efficient LLM architectures. However, existing compression methods are often evaluated with different training setups, tasks, and models, making fair comparison difficult. Meanwhile, the growing use of hybrid Mamba-Transformer architectures raises questions about whether compression strategies transfer across backbones. We present VidToC, a controlled evaluation framework for representative compression algorithms, LLM backbones, and time encoding strategies, covering training-free and fine-tuned settings on three complementary video understanding tasks. Our results reveal task-dependent compression behavior and characterize the effects of compression placement, time encoding, and backbone choice. These findings provide empirical guidance for designing and selecting video token compression strategies across tasks and training settings.

papers.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbf{WeMM-Video}, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL. Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, WeMM-Video demonstrates superior performance in omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, while maintaining highly competitive capabilities across general audio, silent video, image, and text tasks. Specifically, in omni-modal video evaluations, our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art, substantially outperforming proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428 while narrowing the gap with the strong Gemini-3.0-Flash, and our compact WeMM-Video-9B surpasses the larger open-source Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct. We publicly release the WeMM-Video family along with our evaluation and reproduction pipeline to foster further research and development in the open-source community.

papers.title: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Long-form video understanding, as a fundamental yet crucial vision task, is being revolutionized by multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based video agents. However, the retrieval-driven nature inherent to these agents creates a significant bottleneck, forcing them to reactively fetch clips based on local saliency without a global temporal plan. To address this, we present ForeSeek, a foresight-driven video agent that transforms long-video reasoning from reactive retrieval into predictive exploration. Rather than blindly probing the timeline, ForeSeek forms visually grounded expectations over unseen temporal regions, verifies them through targeted observations, and continuously refines its search based on emerging evidence, where failed expectations serve as informative signals for principled backtracking. Furthermore, we develop a two-stage training framework that equips MLLMs with foresight-guided reasoning and efficient decision making. Extensive experiments on five long-video benchmarks demonstrate that ForeSeek consistently improves the efficiency--accuracy trade-off of long-video reasoning, achieving competitive or superior accuracy while observing $2.5$--$4.4\times$ fewer frames than the strongest search-based agent. Code is available at https://github.com/harry0021/ForeSeek

papers.title: DriftGuard: Online Memory-Drift Detection via Causal Attribution for LLM Agents
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on persistent memory to plan tool calls and complete multi-step tasks, which exposes them to memory drift: an adversarial or misleading memory alters the execution path and final outcome. In this work, we investigate online memory-drift detection, which estimates each retrieved memory's causal contribution to potential drift at serving time. We identify two fundamental challenges. (1) Content-level features are insufficient for causal memory-drift attribution, as perplexity or retrieval relevance alone cannot determine which retrieved memory would change agent behavior if neutralized; (2) Counterfactual attribution is prohibitively expensive for online detection, as it requires replaying downstream agent and tool execution for each candidate memory, exceeding real-time serving budgets. To address these challenges, we propose DriftGuard, a two-stage framework that decouples offline causal supervision from online estimation. Specifically, DriftGuard first constructs causal supervision through repeated paired counterfactual replays, continuing the original and single-memory neutralized trajectory suffixes from a shared pre-action state. The resulting annotations are aggregated by component-wise majority voting into a memory drift score (MDS) that captures action change, attack removal, violation removal, and task recovery. Guided by this supervision, DriftGuard then learns an online risk model that estimates MDS from pre-action information and flags drift-inducing memories via its maximum component risk, without online counterfactual rollouts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DriftGuard accurately identifies drift-inducing memories and enables efficient online defense. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DriftGuard-7F0B.

papers.title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is moving from the harness of prompts and tools around a base model toward the model itself. However, existing RSI still faces key challenges, including harness-bound gains that stay outside the base model, black-box supervision that reads only the model's outputs, and imprecise edits whose site and strength are fixed in advance. To address these challenges, we propose BaseRSI, a new paradigm of Recursive Harness Internalization: the base model improves its harness, then writes what the harness adds into its own weights through training-free edits, round after round on its own responses. To support this paradigm, we introduce ReGap, a mechanism that supervises every transformer block with the high-dimensional activation difference that the harness makes at that block alone, and updates the block's weights along this signal in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this mechanism, we further propose ReKey, an algorithm that writes this signal by regression into a few key-value neurons of every block, and measures the site and strength of each edit on the model's own responses. Moreover, the base model fills every role of this recursion with forward passes alone, and its edits, written at different sites, compose in one checkpoint without refitting. Experimental results on ten visual reasoning benchmarks show that BaseRSI consistently improves a base vision-language model both in distribution and on held-out benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/BaseRSI.

papers.title: Fold the Loop: Decoding-Time KV Memory for Looped Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Looped vision-language models (VLMs) deepen visual reasoning by repeatedly applying weight-tied modules. However, their decoding memory grows with recurrent depth and limits the image size and batch size that fit in a fixed memory budget. Each recurrent step produces its own key-value (KV) states, so the cache holds several copies of the same image. We find that, after an exact prefill, earlier steps still need access to visual information but can reuse the final visual KV within the same module. We propose FoldCache, which compresses visual KV along the recurrent axis while preserving the full prefill computation. FoldCache partitions recurrent steps within each module into groups and retains the final visual KV of each group for its members to share during decoding. Sharing stays within module boundaries, while question and answer KV remain separate for each step. The grouping granularity controls the degree of compression, and folding can be combined with token eviction and quantization to further reduce memory use. On LoopVL, FoldCache approximately halves prefix KV memory while matching full-cache accuracy on five open-ended benchmarks. These memory savings support batch sizes up to 1.7 times those of a full cache under the same GPU memory budget, and up to 2.6 times with the more aggressive FoldCache-Lite.

papers.title: Keep the Reasoning, Read the Image: On-Demand Visual KV for Multi-Turn Reasoning VLMs
papers.abstract_en: Reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) think for thousands of tokens before they answer, and retention policies keep the KV cache affordable by pruning it as the reasoning grows. We find that this pruning sacrifices the image in multi-turn conversations: the image and the reasoning share one budget, so the growing reasoning crowds the visual entries out. A chart question that loses 8 points to the full cache when asked first loses 24 points when asked after a round of reasoning. Protecting a small visual reserve from eviction recovers most of this loss, while adding the same slots to the shared budget recovers considerably less. The image therefore lacks protection, not capacity. Based on this finding, we propose ShelfKV, a training-free method that works on top of existing retention policies. It keeps every visual entry in CPU memory and, at each decoding step, swaps the visual entries that the current query scores highest into the attention slots of the text entries it scores lowest. The image is never evicted, yet it occupies attention slots only while it is read. We evaluate ShelfKV on four benchmarks, three of them conversational, with two retention policies and two reasoning VLMs. In conversations, it improves the strongest existing policy, DBTrimKV, by up to 20.3 points at matched GPU memory, and still leads by 8.7 points when DBTrimKV uses twice the memory. It also consistently outperforms a fixed visual reserve of matched GPU memory in these settings, without hurting accuracy on standalone questions. These results show that the image should be protected from the reasoning but read only on demand.

papers.title: Thinking in Streams: Proactive Spatial Reasoning with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Recognizing when a requested spatial condition holds in streaming video can require maintaining and updating spatial knowledge across changing viewpoints. We study this capability through proactive spatial reasoning, where a model receives a query in advance and determines whether and when to respond as the stream unfolds. We introduce ProSpace-Bench, comprising nine tasks across object, camera, and scene reasoning, and ProSpace-Train for supervised training. To support spatial decisions, we propose ProSpace-VLM, which injects explicit geometric encodings estimated causally from incoming frames into intermediate VLM layers, using the existing KV cache as spatial memory and spatial token selection for efficient streaming. Experiments reveal a substantial gap between VLMs and humans, while ProSpace-VLM improves timely responses and correct abstention over fine-tuned baselines. Analyses examine how ProSpace-VLM represents previously observed spatial information across changing viewpoints.

papers.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract_en: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) enables a single student to absorb the skills of several domain teachers by learning from its own generated responses. We present Multimodal Model Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation Reasoner (M3OPD-Reasoner), a fully open recipe for post-training vision-language models (VLMs) over three reasoning domains: image STEM, image perception, and video. We curate two datasets, M3OPD-SFT-1.35M for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and M3OPD-RL-193K for reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards. On these data, we compare post-training recipes that start from Qwen3.5-9B: training one model on the mixed data of all domains (MixSFT and MixRL), and training one teacher per domain with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO), directly or after an SFT warm-up, and distilling the teachers into one student with MOPD. We evaluate on 21 image STEM, image perception, and video reasoning benchmarks after we decontaminate the training data against them. The comparison establishes MOPD of teachers trained with GSPO directly from Qwen3.5-9B as the best recipe: the student closely matches each teacher on its own domain and is on average above the mixed-training baselines on the same prompts. Since MOPD already merges the domain capabilities that MixRL would otherwise have to learn, its student is a stronger starting point for RL, and we ask whether the same data can carry the model further from there: we add MixRL on top of the MOPD student, on the same prompts and with the same settings, which, to our knowledge, no prior VLM recipe has studied. The same prompts still improve the MOPD student, with no collapse, and give our main model, M3OPD-Reasoner-9B. MOPD and MixRL can therefore work as consecutive stages that get more out of the same data. We release all data, the training code, and the checkpoints of every stage.

papers.title: MoGloss: Joint Motion and Pseudo-Gloss Pretraining for American Sign Language Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Sign language translation and recognition have been shown to benefit from various pretraining approaches. We propose a novel two-stage pretraining approach for the motion encoder, which first learns to reconstruct masked motion, followed by joint masked prediction of pseudo-gloss units and motion. Pseudo-glosses serve as an intermediate structured representation of natural language text and are obtained from the captions by a large language model. We curate a corpus of about 1,100 hours of American Sign Language from five public datasets, estimate 2D pose for all clips and define an evaluation protocol. We then reproduce state-of-the-art translation methods and evaluate them using the same train and test splits. We propose a translation model built on our pretraining strategy, and this model outperforms the previous state-of-the-art methods Uni-Sign and SHuBERT, as well as the YouTube-ASL baseline, on the How2Sign, ASL STEM Wiki and OpenASL datasets. Furthermore, the gain from the joint pretraining using motion and pseudo-gloss grows as translation data shrinks. A classifier built on the same encoder also achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on ASL Citizen isolated sign recognition and outperforms our reproduction of Uni-Sign on WLASL2000.

papers.title: AggCLIP: Aggregating CLIP for Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract_en: Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection (ZSMAD) aims to identify both appearance and geometric defects in novel categories without relying on target-specific training data, making it especially valuable in real-world scenarios constrained by data scarcity, privacy concerns, or high annotation costs. While recent approaches successfully adapt vision-language models like CLIP to achieve this open-vocabulary generalization, they still face significant challenges: (i) severe geometric information loss during 3D-to-2D point cloud rendering; (ii) spatially noisy 2D feature maps produced by raw CLIP patch embeddings, compounded by shallow late-stage modality fusion; and (iii) severe cross-modal semantic misalignment due to decoupled processing streams. To address these limitations, we propose AggCLIP, a novel framework that adapts frozen CLIP representations for ZSMAD by explicitly incorporating local geometric structure and visual spatial context. Specifically, to accurately localize fine-grained defects, we design a Geometry-Aware Spatial Aggregation (GSA) module that refines back-projected 3D point features via density-adaptive neighborhood weighting, alongside a Context-Aware Spatial Aggregation (CSA) module that smooths multi-scale 2D patch embeddings using a lightweight trainable adapter. Furthermore, to prevent semantic drift between modalities, we introduce a Dual-Stream Prompt Contrastive (DSPC) loss, which aligns the abstract concepts of normality and abnormality across the point cloud and RGB streams. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed AggCLIP framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies benchmarks under both one-vs-rest and cross-dataset zero-shot settings, notably surpassing the strongest competitive methods by up to 2.9% in pixel-level AUPRO.

papers.title: CROMPT: Adapting CLIP via Cross-Modal Prompting for Robust Zero-Shot Generalization under Adverse Weather
papers.abstract_en: Domain adaptation for semantic segmentation is challenging when target-domain images are unavailable during training. Zero-shot domain adaptation addresses this by adapting models using only textual descriptions of the target domain. However, existing prompt-learning methods are not well suited for ResNet-based CLIP vision backbones or pixel-level cross-modal feature alignment. We propose CROMPT, a prompt-learning framework for zero-shot domain adaptation in semantic segmentation. CROMPT introduces Cross-Modal Feature Augmentation (CROMA), combining Random Visual Prompting with Hybrid Textual Prompting (HTP) to jointly adapt visual and textual representations. We further propose CROMA-VL, which leverages vision-language models to generate domain-conditioned prompts, and a progressive easy-to-hard adaptation strategy for improved domain invariance. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines and state-of-the-art methods, achieving 1.63-2.63% mIoU gains while maintaining inference-time complexity. These results establish CROMPT as an effective and efficient framework for zero-shot multi-domain semantic segmentation. OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=FxqFsIL685

papers.title: ResVision: Spectrum-Matched Resizing and Context-Preserving Inspection for Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Agentic visual reasoning improves vision-language models by selectively enlarging evidence without adding new scene content, but the benefit depends on whether fine structure remains accessible and whether local observations stay grounded in the full scene. We identify three recurring bottlenecks: high-frequency detail can be attenuated during visual-token formation; spatially distributed evidence can remain encoded yet difficult for the language model to retrieve; and isolated crops can weaken whole-detail correspondence through scale and positional mismatch. ResVision addresses these limitations with two complementary components. Spectrum-Matched Resizing (SMR) estimates image complexity and selects an adaptive global sampling scale, avoiding unnecessary enlargement on simple inputs while allocating more visual tokens to detail-rich images. Context-Preserving Inspection (CPI) returns each inspected crop together with the complete working view, preserving local detail and global context across tool turns. We evaluate Direct and Agentic variants on four frontier VLMs and 29 benchmarks spanning six visual-reasoning families. Complete ResVision (Agentic Base plus SMR plus CPI) is best for every model, improving by 3.36 to 4.94 points over Direct Base and 1.87 to 2.94 points over Agentic Base. These results show that adaptive visual sampling and context-preserving inspection address distinct, complementary constraints in multimodal reasoning.

papers.title: MultiBinder: Preventing Multi-Subject Identity Leakage in Personalized Video Generation
papers.abstract_en: Personalized video generation faces a significant scalability challenge: as the number of custom subjects increases, existing methods suffer from severe identity leakage and semantic entanglement, resulting in videos with blended attributes and incoherent narratives. We identify that this stems from a lack of explicit binding between textual entity phrases and their corresponding visual patterns prior to fusion in diffusion models. To address this, we propose MultiBinder, a novel framework built on a ``bind-then-narrate'' paradigm. Our approach introduces a two-stage conditioning process before video diffusion. First, Cross-modal Entity Binding devises an entity-aware Q-Former to extract identity-centric features from each subject's reference image and tightly align them with its unique entity phrase, yielding disentangled ``identity tokens.'' Second, a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) acts as a ``narrative director'' in the Narrative-Aware Subject Arrangement stage, capturing the action of each subject from the text prompt and synthesizes contextualized subject features that encapsulate ``who is doing what'' and preserve role-specific distinctions. These features are then injected into a video diffusion model via dedicated conditioning pathways, ensuring precise attribute allocation. Extensive experiments on both general and newly curated multi-subject benchmarks show that MultiBinder significantly outperforms existing methods in multi-subject identity fidelity.

papers.title: Keel: A Frontier Model Teaches a Vision-Language Model by Rewriting Its Weights
papers.abstract_en: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs on image tasks, finds and removes it there. Told only the symptom, an editor, a frontier multimodal LLM acting as an agent, locates the cause, edits the weights and tests them, with a failure census and instruments showing it the failing images and where the VLM attends; among several editors, the harness keeps only edits that clearly reduce the failure without lowering accuracy on questions no editor saw. The repair needs no training, keeps the model's size and per-token cost, and applies to already-edited weights. The editors expose where the loops live: from the original weights, independent editors on both models trace them to the attention outputs of the middle layers, and the smaller VLM stops consulting the image inside a loop. On Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-2B, across six image benchmarks from visual mathematics to GUI grounding, the edit removes most loops on every benchmark and shortens answers, and the edited models are significantly more accurate than the thinking models on average; the larger one gains most on GUI grounding, a task absent from the practice questions. Because the repair lives in the weights, it combines with budget forcing where held-out questions favor it: on the best available weights, Keel has the best average accuracy on both models, significantly above every training-free baseline we compare on the larger one.

papers.title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
papers.abstract_en: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, then fine-tunes a target model on the resulting trajectories. We introduce AutoMaster, an autonomous post-training system in which an LLM agent develops these interventions through trajectory analysis, skill design, data selection, and feedback from rollouts and target-model evaluation. Across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks with 4B and 9B target models, AutoMaster improves mean performance over Vanilla SFT on successful unguided teacher trajectories by 1.42-8.99 percentage points, with the teacher, task pool, training set size, and SFT recipe held fixed. Together with the ablations and trajectory analyses, these results suggest that behavioral shaping can make a fixed model a more effective teacher. We further find that retaining skill instructions during SFT yields higher mean performance than removing them across all six settings, despite their absence at evaluation and identical supervised outputs. These findings suggest that preserving skill context as part of a training demonstration can support better behavioral internalization.

papers.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few evaluation datasets leads to systematically over-optimistic performance estimates. We further demonstrate that compute-optimal scaling requires expanding the range of synthetic pretraining dataset sizes alongside model size and training compute. Increasing the maximum numbers of rows and features sampled during pretraining improves performance and produces more predictable scaling trends. These insights guide the training of more efficient TabPFNv2-like models, using the open-source training pipeline of nanoTabPFN.

papers.title: Let a Small Model Read First: Faster Prefill for Long Interleaved Image-Text Inputs
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about long interleaved inputs, such as documents of many pages and collections of hundreds of images, but they are slow to start: on inputs of about 100K tokens, the prefill takes most of the wait for the first output token. A common approach prunes the input by scoring its tokens with the target model itself or with a small model of the same family that first writes an answer. However, this scoring takes much of the time that pruning saves. We find that the evidence for a question lies in a few whole units (images or paragraphs), and that a small hybrid model finds them with one attention head of an early layer, even at half image resolution. Based on these findings, we propose SkimPrefill, which lets the small hybrid model read the whole input first, up to that early layer, with images at half resolution. Most layers of the small hybrid model (Qwen3.5-0.8B) run in linear time, so this pass is short. SkimPrefill then ranks every unit with that head and gives the target the top units as an ordinary shorter prompt. One untrained selector serves targets of different model families. Extensive experiments on MMLongBench at 128K tokens, with 19 datasets of five task types, show the effectiveness of SkimPrefill. With 10% of the input tokens kept, SkimPrefill speeds up the prefill of Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma-4-12B and Qwen3-VL-32B by 3.7 times, 11.6 time and 8.2 times while maintaining their average accuracy.

papers.title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting problem, jointly optimizing partition boundaries and local models through dynamic programming. The resulting adaptive temporal partitions guide frame budget allocation based on query relevance and temporal extent, enabling informative frame selection under limited visual budgets. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that APS consistently improves performance across diverse LVLM backbones, achieving the highest average gains over uniform sampling among competing methods. Further analyses validate the effectiveness of adaptive partitioning and demonstrate its generalizability across model scales, similarity encoders, and advanced LVLMs.

papers.title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are more prevalent, our work opens the door to a more focused diagnosis of their strategic reasoning errors. For illustrative purposes, we offer an interactive visualizer of our methodology on selected sample traces at https://interp-self.github.io/gametrace/

papers.title: Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders
papers.abstract_en: In latent diffusion models, expanding the latent dimension of variational autoencoders (VAEs) is essential to push the upper bound of reconstruction quality. However, without explicit structural constraints, such unregularized expansion easily yields a rugged and ill-conditioned latent manifold, causing generated latents to drift off the manifold during generation (i.e., off-manifold problem). Recent works smooth this manifold by using external foundation models (e.g., DINOv2) as a topological regularizer. However, we argue that tying the latent space to frozen external priors inherently restricts generalization: bound by their pre-training distributions and semantic biases, they may fail to capture faithful visual details on out-of-distribution domains. Observing that low-dimensional latents naturally form a smoother, generation-friendly manifold, we propose dual-manifold VAE (DM-VAE) to leverage internal representations as a topological regularizer. Specifically, DM-VAE pairs a high-dimensional reconstructive branch with a low-dimensional branch that extracts a clean topological skeleton, anchoring the high-dimensional manifold to this smooth subspace. Building upon this framework, we further introduce topological representation alignment (TRA) to supervise intermediate generator features during training, and internal guidance with topological skeleton (IG_TS) to guide structural components while preserving high-frequency details at inference. On ImageNet-1K (256x256), our foundation-model-free DM-VAE achieves a state-of-the-art rFID of 0.12 and a generation FID50K of 1.28 (w/o CFG) and 1.20 (w/CFG), and further reaches 1.11 when orthogonally combined with DINOv2.

papers.title: Retroactive Concept Bottleneck Models for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning
papers.abstract_en: Exemplar-free class-incremental learning (EFCIL) requires models to learn new classes sequentially without retaining training samples from previous tasks. Continual concept bottleneck models (CBMs) make their predictions interpretable by identifying visual concepts in an image and using them to score each class. However, these methods typically focus on preserving learned concepts or approximating past classes with generated features, which can leave new concepts underused in old-class predictions. We propose RetroCBM, which retains a small set of vocabulary-independent statistics relating frozen visual features to the embedding space of a pretrained vision-language model. Even after earlier training images have been discarded, we can use these statistics to supervise new concepts. To do so, we develop a retroactive regression rule that yields the same predictor for each new concept as class-balanced ridge regression on all images seen so far. We then reproject the stored statistics to recover the full-history squared classification loss and thus learn how much each new concept should contribute to old-class predictions. Since the classifier may use systematic concept errors to distinguish nearby classes, we further introduce a graph-weighted penalty on the margin shifts caused by those errors. Across six datasets, RetroCBM outperforms state-of-the-art interpretable methods in all class-incremental settings, with an 18.1\% relative gain in mean average incremental accuracy over the strongest exemplar-free baseline.

papers.title: Stabilizing Neural-to-Image Retrieval with Frequency-Domain Priors and Adaptive Supervision
papers.abstract_en: Visual neural decoding aims to infer perceived visual stimuli from brain activity, offering important insights into human visual cognition while enabling transformative applications in brain computer interfaces and artificial intelligence. Recent advances in pretrained vision-language models have provided a semantically rich representation space for this task. However, reliable alignment between EEG/MEG signals and visual embeddings remains challenging because neural responses are noisy, highly variable across trials, and subject dependent. To address this issue, we propose a unified neural-to-image retrieval framework that improves retrieval performance by aligning neural and image representations in a shared semantic space. The framework integrates dual-stream adaptation, frequency-domain calibration, and phase-guided temperature modulation to promote more robust cross-modal semantic alignment. Specifically, dual-stream adaptation models a low-dimensional shared subspace with correlation regularization to suppress redundant noise and enhance cross-modal consistency. Frequency-domain calibration conditionally modulates neural representations using amplitude and phase statistics. Phase-guided temperature modulation further adjusts the supervision strength in contrastive learning according to the stability of neural responses. Experiments on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG under both intra-subject and inter-subject settings demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms strong baselines. These results suggest that robust neural-to-image retrieval under heterogeneous neural conditions benefits from a stable shared semantic space, frequency-informed representation calibration, and adaptive supervision. Code will be released at github.com/wanfkuabc/Geometry-Regularized-Brain-Embeddings.
